label: Darwinian profile of a scoped epistemic evaluative judgment
term: Darwinian profile of a scoped epistemic evaluative judgment (origin fixing, within-history variation, tracking failure)
definition: A profile supplies scenarios, the selective history of each, a designated actual scenario, and for one scoped epistemic evaluative judgment its Boolean verdict and the correctness of its content in each scenario. A history-mate is a scenario with the actual selective history. Origin fixing: every history-mate has the actual verdict. Within-history variation: some history-mate differs from the actual scenario in correctness. Correctness fixed by history: every history-mate has the actual correctness. Tracking failure: some history-mate has an incorrect verdict. Actual accuracy: the verdict is correct in the actual scenario. Constant correctness: every scenario has the actual correctness. Cross-history verdict variation: some scenario with a different history has a different verdict. Scenario mismatch: some scenario has an incorrect verdict. The uniform mismatch policy says that, for each basis of a subject, a tracking failure of the judgment that basis delivers undercuts that basis in a supplied reliability frame (26cbf25d-f3d5-46ea-91e8-e2140a57b04d).
note: Analyst vocabulary for #1585, attribution deferred. Street 2006 n. 2 and n. 57 only state that the dilemma can be extended to epistemic reasons; this reconstruction is not hers. Origin fixing idealizes her 'tremendous influence' as full determination of the verdict by the history. Tracking failure is a modal condition across history-mates; it does not entail inaccuracy in the actual scenario, but because the actual scenario is a history-mate, actual inaccuracy is a case of it, and so the uniform mismatch policy treats an actually false verdict as undercutting. Undercutting is justified defeat for a subject, not falsity of the content; neither is global epistemic nihilism. Street's own first horn (pp. 121–122, the Bermuda analogy) holds the truths fixed and lets the verdict vary with the history (constant correctness with cross-history verdict variation), then argues from coincidence to likely actual error; within-history variation of correctness is a separate analyst reading, not her horn, and a realism with constant correctness, her paradigm target, fails it. Relation-asserting realisms (correctness supervening on truth-conduciveness that selection responds to) belong to her second horn, which is not formalized here. A source reading of Street's own definition of stance-independence is e1aab5d4-0115-53d3-ab0c-2a3ead63e6d3; it is not identified with within-history variation. No probability, causal mechanism or actual selective history is encoded.
